scope.included: Project-owned image definitions under old/images plus old/orchestrator/dagster/Dockerfile and their build, runner, adapter, and orchestration references.
scope.excluded: Target-repository, scratch-checkout, third-party fixture, and vendored-source Dockerfiles except the ScanCode Dockerfile selected by the project-owned image definition.

acceptance.bash_powershell_selection_parity: passed using Linux container Bash and native PowerShell

notes: The 353 count covers image.json download steps only; downloads performed inside legacy Dockerfiles are not covered by that guarantee.
ScanCode uses an unpinned shallow git clone rather than a download step.
Eight external FROM instructions are not digest-pinned: two in audit-binary-analysis and one each in audit-container, audit-iac, audit-native, audit-static, audit-static-opengrep, and ScanCode.

hadolint.interpretation: Lint findings are engineering signals, not security findings. Most narrow tool images had one warning; build-environment and omnibus definitions account for most findings.

fresh_runtime_probes.boundary: No network, read-only root, all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, uid/gid 10001, bounded pids/memory/cpu, tmpfs only, no target mounts, no Docker socket.
caveats: Build-environment, legacy omnibus, native, and binary-analysis images were checked only with a safe version/startup command.
Tool images were checked with their version or help command; no arbitrary repository was scanned.
Microsoft SBOM Tool initially failed with a 64 MiB /tmp probe and passed with the archived boundary's larger tmpfs allowance.
SpotBugs logged a hostname-resolution error without --add-host and passed cleanly with the archived boundary's hostname mapping.

fresh_build.result: build success and build-time version check success
fresh_build.network: Build steps used --network none, but BuildKit still contacted Docker Hub for Dockerfile frontend and base-image metadata. This is not an offline-build proof.

historical_build_records.interpretation: These records show archived build attempts reported OK; they do not prove current reproducibility, startup, function, or security acceptance.

unverified_gaps: No network research was performed for current upstream support, latest versions, vulnerability status, or license changes; every reused pin must be re-resolved against authoritative upstream sources during porting.
No image vulnerability scan or SBOM/license-policy evaluation was performed.
No arm64 builds or probes were performed; many assets and wheels explicitly target linux/amd64 or x86_64.
No functional target scan was run, and archived scripts were not executed.
Resource ceilings were exercised only as probe limits, not under representative workloads.

strengths: The archived central adapter builds argv arrays without a shell, requires immutable image identities, forces a numeric non-root uid/gid, mounts targets read-only, permits one writable scratch mount, drops all capabilities, sets no-new-privileges, disables pulls and networking by default, applies pids/memory/cpu/tmpfs/time/output limits, and records explicit terminal causes.
Sensitive mount checks reject filesystem roots, user homes, credential directories, run-owned data, and Docker sockets.
No project-owned runtime path was found mounting a Docker socket or using --privileged.
blocking_changes: Port these controls as independently tested runtime code; do not copy archived orchestration wholesale.
Remove or separately authorize the legacy DEBUG_CAPS path that can add SYS_PTRACE and disable the seccomp profile.
Make network policy enforceable by destination or fail closed; the archive reports NETWORK_ENFORCEMENT_UNAVAILABLE when destinations are requested.
Keep output/exit-code adapters beside application jobs, not inside image definitions.

evidence.observation: default network/read-only/capability boundary and the limited unrestricted-build job allow-list
argv-only invocation, immutable image reference, limits, read-only target mounts, and one writable scratch mount
home, credential directory, filesystem-root, run-data, and Docker-socket mount rejection
explicit terminal result, bounded streams, timeout, state inspection, and cleanup
legacy wrapper mirrors most controls but has opt-in bridge networking and debug capability escape hatches
